IX.}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=9|verse=1}}}}ND he said to them, Amen I say to you, that there be some of them that stand here, vvhich shal not tast of death, vntil they see the kingdom of God comming in povver.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 16, 27. 17, 1. Lu. 9, 27.''}} {{verse|chapter=9|verse=2}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the Annotations vpon the 17 of S. Matthew.}}∷ And after six daies {{sc|Iesvs}} taketh Peter and Iames and Iohn: and bringeth them alone into a high mountaine apart, and vvas transfigured before them. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=3}}† And his garments vvere made glistering and vvhite excedingly as snovv, the like vvhereof a fuller cannot make vvhite vpon the earth. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=4}}† And there appeared to them {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The law and the Prophets ioyne with Christ and his Gospel: the one signified by Moyses, the other by Elias. By whose apparitions here we also learne that sometime there may be personal entercourse betwixt the liuing & the dead, though not ordinarily.}}∷ {{sup|‖}} Elias vvith Moyses: and they vvere talking vvith {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=5}}† And Peter ansvvering, said to {{sc|Iesvs}}, Rabbi, it is good for vs to be here: and let vs make three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moyses, and one for Elias. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=6}}† For he knevv not vvhat he said: for they vvere frighted vvith feare: {{verse|chapter=9|verse=7}}† and there vvas a cloude ouershadovving them, and a voice came out of the cloude, saying, This is my Sonne most deere: heare ye him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=8}}† And immediatly looking about, they savv no man any more but {{sc|Iesvs}} only vvith them. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=9}}† And as they descēded from the mountaine, he commaunded them that they should not tel any man vvhat things they had seen: but vvhen the Sonne of man shal be risen againe from the dead. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=10}}† And they kept in the vvord vvith them selues: questioning together vvhat that should be, ''when he shal be risen from the dead''.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=11}}† And they asked him, saying, What say the Pharisees then and the Scribes, that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mal. 4, 5.''}}* Elias must come first? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=12}}† Who ansvvering said to them, Elias vvhen he commeth first, shal restore al things: and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`as''}}`hovv' it is vvritten of the Sonne of man, that he shal suffer many things and be contemned. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=13}}† But I say to you that {{sup|‖}} Elias also is come (and they haue done to him vvhatsoeuer they vvould) as it is vvritten of him.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=14}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 17, 14. Lu. 9, 37.''}}* cōming to his Disciples, he savv a great multitude about them, and the Scribes questioning vvith them. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=15}}† And forthvvith al the people seeing {{sc|Iesvs}}, vvas astonied, and much afraid: and running to him, saluted him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=16}}† And he asked them, What do you question of among you? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=17}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō wenesday in the Imber weeke of September.}}And one of the multitude ansvvering, said, Maister, I haue brought my sonne to thee, hauing a dumme spirit, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=18}}† Who, vvheresoeuer he taketh him, dasheth him, and he fometh, and gnasheth vvith the teeth, and vvithereth: and I spake to thy Disciples to cast him out, and they could not. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=19}}† Who ansvvering them,<noinclude>{{rh|||said,}}</noinclude>
